article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid
Genetics: Forum Cookies × Face Off OG BX1
Breeder: Archive Seed Bank
THC Content: 18–27%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: Myrcene , beta-caryophyllene , humulene
Primary Flavors: Cookie dough, skunky Kush, earth
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: early to mid October
Indoor Yield: 300–400 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 400–600 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy to intermediate

Samoas began with a familiar piece of elite California cannabis and deliberately made it heavier, louder, and more productive. Archive Seed Bank crossed the Forum cut of Girl Scout Cookies with its Face Off OG breeding line, creating a hybrid that retained the unusual appearance and sweet baked character of Forum Cookies while reinforcing the parts some growers felt the original clone lacked. More yield, greater potency, stronger Kush funk, and a somewhat quicker finish were central to the project. Archive has even described growers replacing their Forum Cookies cut with Samoas because the hybrid could deliver much of the same exotic appeal while producing substantially more flower.

The result bears little resemblance to the coconut-heavy dessert its name might suggest. Cookie dough and sweetness are present, but mature flowers can smell equally strongly of skunky Kush, earth, chocolate, berries, nuts, and chemical diesel. Effects likewise avoid a simple indica-or-sativa label. The first stage is generally euphoric and mentally engaging, while a thicker physical relaxation builds underneath as the high develops. Dense trichomes, green-and-purple flower coloration, balanced hybrid effects, and roughly nine weeks of flowering have helped keep this cultivar relevant long after the first wave of Cookies crosses flooded the marijuana market.
Genetics and Lineage

The direct pedigree is Forum Cookies × Face Off OG BX1. Forum Cookies refers to the famous Forum-selected Girl Scout Cookies clone, one of the cuts that helped turn Cookies genetics into a global cannabis category. Its strengths lie in dense resin, unusual flower structure, sweet baked aromatics, earthy mint, and a potent hybrid effect. Its weaknesses from a grower’s perspective include relatively modest yield and a structure that can be less commercially productive than its reputation might imply. Archive chose Face Off OG specifically to address those shortcomings without stripping away the traits that made the Forum cut desirable.

Face Off OG represents one of the central foundations of Archive Seed Bank’s breeding program. The original plant traces back to seeds found in particularly powerful Southern California OG Kush flower circulating in the late 1990s. Archive selected the #4 plant for its unusual OG flavor and exceptionally strong high, then developed backcross generations around that mother. Bringing the BX1 into Forum Cookies intensified the OG side of Samoas: more earth, fuel, Skunk, Kush, stronger physical potency, and better flower production than the Cookies clone typically delivers on its own.

This pairing also makes Samoas closely related in breeding philosophy to Do-Si-Dos , another influential Archive Cookies × Face Off OG project. Both cultivars were designed to reinforce elite Cookies material with the breeder’s prized OG line rather than bury it beneath unrelated genetics. In Samoas, the Forum cut remains easy to recognize in the appearance and sweet terpene profile, while Face Off OG supplies the muscular structure and darker Kush personality that give the hybrid its own identity.
Effects and Experience

The opening phase tends to favor the cerebral side of the genetics. Mood can rise quickly, and conversation, games, music, movies, or other forms of entertainment may become more immersive. Mental activity often remains lively enough for the cultivar to feel creative or sociable at moderate amounts, but the effect is richer and more physically grounded than the light, purely energetic high associated with many sativa-leaning strains . A slightly dreamy quality can develop as the initial euphoria expands, making the experience enjoyable without necessarily improving precision or concentration.

Physical pressure becomes increasingly obvious later. The Face Off OG influence gives the high a dense, enveloping quality that can spread through the shoulders and limbs while the earlier cerebral stimulation gradually becomes calmer. At moderate doses, that transition creates a particularly balanced experience: mentally pleasant but physically relaxed, with neither side immediately dominating. Larger quantities can change the equation considerably, bringing appetite, heavier limbs, reduced motivation, and eventually pronounced sedation in sensitive consumers.

Documented THC values commonly fall between approximately 18% and 27%, but one number should never be treated as permanent chemistry for a seed line. Different phenotypes and growing environments can produce noticeably different cannabinoid concentrations. Stronger examples can become surprisingly intense, especially because the Cookies sweetness may make the smoke feel gentler than the eventual high. Excess consumption can result in anxiety, dizziness, short-term memory impairment, dry mouth, or excessive sleepiness.
Medical Benefits

The shift from cerebral uplift into full-body calm may appeal to some medical marijuana consumers who want relaxation without starting from an immediately sleepy state. People sometimes gravitate toward balanced Cookies-and-OG hybrids for discomfort, stress, appetite loss, or difficulty unwinding in the evening because the experience can remain mentally pleasant while physical tension gradually softens. The tendency for appetite to become more noticeable later in the session may also be relevant for some consumers.

Samoas itself has not been tested in controlled clinical trials, however, and the effects of a named cannabis cultivar should not be treated as established medical treatment. Research involving cannabinoids more broadly has found potential benefit for certain forms of chronic pain, nausea, and several other symptoms, but responses depend on dose, cannabinoid ratios, method of administration, individual physiology, and other medications. Flower testing near the upper end of the documented THC range may behave very differently from standardized cannabinoid products used in medical research.

The same properties that feel soothing to one person can become counterproductive to another. Higher THC exposure can increase anxiety, interfere with concentration, impair coordination, or produce more sedation than intended. Consumers using weed for health-related reasons should therefore pay attention to current laboratory testing and personal sensitivity rather than relying solely on the reputation of Forum Cookies or Face Off OG.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The first impression is usually darker and more Kush-heavy than the name suggests. Cookie dough and earthy sweetness appear immediately, but the Face Off parent brings enough skunk, fuel, and pungent OG resin to prevent the aroma from becoming a straightforward dessert profile. Breaking apart a mature flower can uncover chocolate, berries, toasted nuts, mint, damp earth, and chemical diesel, with different expressions emphasizing either the sweeter Forum side or the sharper OG half of the cross.

Smoking or vaporizing the flower reveals even more contrast. Sweet cookie and cocoa-like notes may lead the inhale before earthy Kush and diesel build through the middle. Berry sweetness can brighten selected phenotypes, while mint and nuttiness create the closest connection to the famous cookie whose name inspired this weed strain . The finish is generally heavier, lingering with skunky earth and fuel rather than disappearing into sugar.

Breeder-cut cultivation records have associated the profile with myrcene, beta-caryophyllene, and humulene, a combination that fits the earthy, peppery, herbal, and Kush-oriented side particularly well. Terpene concentrations are not genetically fixed, so different crops may express additional compounds or change their relative dominance. A patient dry and cure are especially important because the chocolate, berry, mint, and cookie nuances can fade quickly if the flowers are dried too aggressively, leaving mostly earth and fuel behind.
Growing Information

Samoas was bred in part to improve on the horticultural limitations of Forum Cookies. Archive specifically emphasizes increased yield and a shorter flowering period, while grow observations describe a robust, bushy plant with broad leaves and enough lateral growth to build a productive canopy. Around 60–65 days of flowering is common, placing the cultivar near nine weeks and making it faster than many OG-influenced hybrids. Indoor production of roughly 300–400 grams per square meter has been documented from breeder-cut material, although actual harvest weight changes substantially with lighting, plant count, training, and vegetative time.

The plant’s natural bushiness makes topping and horizontal training useful when cultivation is legal. Rather than allowing interior branches to stack tightly together, opening the canopy can improve light penetration and help more flower sites develop evenly. Mature buds can become dense and resinous, often showing earthy green coloration with streaks of purple beneath heavy trichome coverage. These compact flowers benefit from strong airflow late in bloom, since resin and density can trap moisture even when the plant itself appears vigorous.

Outdoor production has been documented around 400–600 grams per plant under favorable conditions, with harvest generally falling in early to mid-autumn depending on latitude and the exact phenotype. Root volume, sun exposure, seasonal temperatures, and rainfall can shift those numbers dramatically. The cultivar is adaptable enough for indoor or outdoor gardens, but cooler and wetter autumn regions should pay particular attention to dense colas as harvest approaches. A slow post-harvest dry is equally valuable; preserving the sweeter Cookie and berry aromatics keeps the finished flower from becoming dominated entirely by its skunky OG side.
FAQ
What is the genetics of Samoas?

Samoas was bred by Archive Seed Bank from Forum Cookies crossed with Face Off OG BX1. The Forum Cookies side supplies the exotic Cookies appearance and sweet baked aroma, while Face Off OG adds potency, yield, Kush funk, and stronger physical effects.
Is Samoas indica or sativa?

It is generally considered a balanced hybrid, around 50% indica and 50% sativa. The effects often reflect that balance by starting euphoric and mentally engaging before becoming progressively more relaxing through the body.
How strong is Samoas?

Documented breeder-cut material commonly falls around 18–27% THC. Actual strength varies by phenotype and cultivation conditions, with stronger examples capable of producing a powerful and long-lasting high.
What does Samoas taste like?

The flavor combines cookie dough, earthy Kush, chocolate, berries, toasted nuts, mint, Skunk, and diesel. Some plants lean sweeter and more Cookies-like, while others emphasize the fuel-heavy Face Off OG side.
How long does Samoas take to flower?

Most cultivation references place the flowering period around 8–9 weeks, commonly 60–65 days. The Face Off OG influence helped shorten flowering compared with the original Forum Cookies clone while also increasing production.
Final Thoughts on Samoas

Samoas illustrates why Archive Seed Bank’s Face Off OG breeding work became so influential. Instead of replacing the personality of Forum Cookies, the breeder reinforced it where the original cut could be improved. The hybrid keeps the exotic resin-coated appearance, cookie sweetness, and unusual aromatic complexity while adding more weight, darker Kush terpenes, stronger potency, and better production.

The contrast in flavor is particularly memorable. Sweet dough, chocolate, berries, nuts, and mint create the dessert side, but skunky OG, damp earth, and diesel continually pull the profile back toward classic cannabis . That tension keeps the flower from tasting like another generic Cookies cross and gives different phenotypes room to lean either toward the sweeter mother or the heavier Face Off side.

Cultivation traits make the genetics considerably more practical than the Forum cut by itself. A roughly 60–65-day flowering cycle, bushy growth, documented indoor production around 300–400 g/m², and outdoor potential near 400–600 g per plant give growers meaningful yield without demanding an unusually long schedule. Dense, frosty flowers still require thoughtful airflow and post-harvest handling, but the plant is generally manageable enough for cultivators with basic canopy experience.

The finished high brings the two parents together just as effectively as the plant structure and flavor. Euphoria and mental engagement arrive first, then deeper body relaxation, appetite, and potential sedation emerge with time and dose. That mixture of Forum Cookies character, Face Off OG power, stronger yields, and pronounced skunky-Kush depth is what has allowed Samoas to remain one of Archive Seed Bank’s recognizable Cookies hybrids years after the category became crowded.
